# Most observations fall between 10 and 20

These small synthetic samples demonstrate the chart contract. The table and CSV actions retain individual observations, while a histogram readout describes an interval summary.

```chart
type: histogram
title: The middle intervals contain most observations
data:
  inline:
    - value: 8
    - value: 10
    - value: 12
    - value: 14
    - value: 15
    - value: 16
    - value: 18
    - value: 22
encoding: {x: value}
binning: {edges: [5, 10, 15, 20, 25]}
axes:
  x: {label: Duration, unit: ms}
```

## Unequal intervals need an explicit measure

Each of the next two intervals contains two observations. The wider interval has half the density, so both rectangles have the same area.

```chart
type: histogram
title: Equal probability occupies unequal interval widths
data:
  inline:
    - value: 0
    - value: 0.5
    - value: 1
    - value: 3
encoding: {x: value}
binning: {edges: [0, 1, 3], measure: density}
```

## Compare panels with shared boundaries

Both panels retain the same intervals. Hiding a group removes its contribution and recalculates proportions among the remaining visible observations in that panel. The missing observation stays in the source table and is disclosed below its chart.

```chart
type: histogram
title: The later sample occupies higher intervals
data:
  inline:
    - value: 0
      group: A
      sample: Earlier
    - value: 10
      group: B
      sample: Earlier
    - value: 15
      group: A
      sample: Earlier
    - value: 15
      group: B
      sample: Later
    - value: 20
      group: B
      sample: Later
    - value: 30
      group: A
      sample: Later
    - value: null
      group: A
      sample: Later
encoding: {x: value, color: group, facet: sample}
binning: {count: 3, measure: proportion}
```
